Done: keyfence now has -api-key-file, and reads $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY/api-key without being asked so systemd LoadCredential works (keyfence commit bfde53c). The shipped unit uses it.
Done: docs/demo.gif is shown at the top of the README (commit 2aa1997).
Moved to keyfence's own tracker as keyfence-lls, now that keyfence has one. The fix is entirely in keyfence's code.
Moved to keyfence's tracker as keyfence-0rk. Needs broker-side SO_PEERCRED support; scute's half is just passing the cgroup.

Fixed in keyfence cdc80e0. Over the 10 MiB inspection limit the prefix is spliced back in front of the rest of the stream and the whole response goes to the client with Content-Length untouched; rules are skipped rather than run on a fragment, and the audit trail records that with rule_action 'skipped' and a reason. A response with no rules to run is no longer buffered at all.

Covered by the repository's first Go tests (5, in internal/proxy/response_test.go), which were checked against the previous code to confirm they fail on it -- declared-length and chunked oversized cases, inspection still happening under the limit, rule state still accumulating, and no buffering when there is nothing to inspect. CI runs go test ./... now.

Fixed in keyfence: an empty destination list now permits nothing, issuance refuses an omitted or empty list with a 400 naming ['*'] as the explicit alternative, and the SSH bastion refuses a wildcard. Scute was already safe here -- it requires a non-empty list and rejects '*' -- so nothing changes on this side.

Fixed in keyfence: the bastion now authenticates upstream hosts against a known_hosts file instead of ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey, refusing unknown hosts and mismatched keys with distinct audit reasons. -ssh-insecure-host-keys is the explicit waiver.

Fixed in keyfence 101cfb6 both ways: a reaper forgets credential material once no valid token references it (at once on revoke, within a minute for expiry), and credentials can now be registered by name so scute-minted tokens need not copy a secret in at all.

Both halves done. The README stopped claiming address-level enforcement in 4e3156d; this commit makes it true where the BPF guard can be installed: naming a proxy binds its address as well as its port, adding to any explicit allow list rather than replacing it, and leaving the plan alone where the capability is absent. --dry-run reports which level is in force. Three tests, both branches exercised regardless of the host's capabilities.

The audit trail records connect events from the same observations learn --network collects: {"event": "connect", "address": "1.1.1.1", "port": 53}, only when a policy asks. refuse-unimplemented-controls is empty now; the two tests that pinned the refusal assert the new behaviour. Verified on a real run.
Done in a7fe43e: the README's broker section installs the keyfence package and enables its socket units; releng/keyfence.service stays as the from-source fallback.

A policy can name a credential the broker holds with ref = "name" instead of secret-file. Scute then opens no file and sends a name, so plaintext lives in one process rather than two. Both-or-neither is refused; --dry-run reports the registration rather than a path. Verified end to end against the shipped systemd unit: 200 from api.anthropic.com, real key absent from the sandbox.

Fixed in keyfence 34695f1: a request with no declared length is read up to MaxBodyBytes+1 and denied past it, forwarded intact with a known length within it, and nothing is buffered when no limit is set. Four tests; the two that matter fail against the old code.

The integration suite now runs keyfence with --api-key-file and authenticates all twelve control calls, and a new test 0 asserts that minting without the key is refused with 401. The --insecure-api workaround is gone.

keyfence serves its CA at GET /ca (b98c052); scute fetches it per run, writes it where the sandbox can read it, and removes it afterwards, falling back to the old path for a broker that does not answer. Verified against a broker with a non-default data dir: 200 from upstream where the same setup previously failed with a TLS error.

Fixed in keyfence 491290f: the CONNECT tunnel loops over requests, upstream requests share one transport with an idle pool (a client certificate gets its own, closed afterwards), and responses without a length or chunked framing are chunked on the way out so the client can tell where they end. Measured: connects=1 then connects=0 for two requests, against 1 and 1 before. Four tests on the framing decision.
--with now splits its command the way a shell would (single quotes, double quotes, backslash escapes) and nothing more: no expansion, globbing or operators. Nine cases tested.
The image is dumped to scute.new via SCUTE_IMAGE_OUTPUT and renamed into place by the Makefile. Verified by killing a build mid-dump: the previous binary was intact afterwards.

Not fixable as posed, and the reason is now in the README and in commit a351bc0.

Saving and restoring the disposition with sigaction works at the kernel level -- the struct comes back byte for byte -- but SBCL dispatches all signals through one trampoline and looks the Lisp function up in a table it does not expose. enable-interrupt and %install-handler both answer NIL, so the caller's handler cannot be read back; restoring the kernel struct would leave scute's own forwarder installed with dead state behind it, which is worse than the default.

If it ever matters, the fix is a caller-supplied restore hook, not introspection. Nothing to do for scute the command.

Every token minted for a run carries the same task id; the broker's events come back carrying it and are written into the same JSONL trail as scute's observations. On failure, what the broker refused is reported beside the command's own failure -- the answer that previously required reading the service journal. keyfence gained GET /audit (bounded ring, ?task_id=) and stopped putting token values in the trail: ids are now hashed rather than being the first half of the token.
